messages:
alex: Heads up — several customers hit SSO failures right after last night's IdP cert rotation. Getting a mix of SAML signature errors and 403s from SCIM deprovisioning. Not good.

mira: Which IdP? Okta or AAD? Any correlation to Dedicated vs Hosted customers?

alex: Mostly Okta so far, a couple AAD. Both hosted and dedicated affected. Error seen on the proxy when validating the assertion: 

alex: ```
ERROR: saml: signature verification failed: crypto/rsa: verification error
request_id=abc123 tenant=acme-corp
```

sam: SCIM side shows 403s for delete calls with a body: 

sam: ```
403 Forbidden - service_account_decrypt_error
{"error":"KMS: failed to unwrapKey: invalid header"}
```

jordan: That KMS msg is odd — SCIM (service) shouldn't be decrypting SAML. Could be encrypted attributes that we decrypt for account matching. Did the cert rotation include a JWE header change on the IdP side?

alex: idp-bot posted the rotation at 00:12 UTC: "Okta cert rotate v2026-03-20". I haven't seen a JWE header change note.

idp-bot: :information_source: Okta rotation job completed for tenant "okta-global" at 00:12 UTC. New cert thumbprint: 0x9A3F... No JWE variation logged.

mira: Can someone paste the raw SAML response (sanitized)? Need to check NameID and Recipient/Audience fields. If NameID format changed from persistent->transient that can break matching and then SCIM tries to deprov a non-existent user -> 403 + decrypt path.

alex: Pasted minimal sanitized response: 

alex: ```
<samlp:Response ...>
  <saml:Assertion>
    <saml:Subject>
      <saml:NameID Format=\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent\">abc-uid-123</saml:NameID>
    </saml:Subject>
    <ds:Signature>...</ds:Signature>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
```

sam: Signature looks present. The verification error could be our signature verifier expecting RSA-SHA256 but IdP rotated to RSA-SHA1 (legacy). Check algorithm in SignatureMethod.

jordan: Also confirm the SP metadata we have cached. We had a metadata refresh earlier this week that should pick up new certs, but our SP-to-IdP trust bundle could be stale on some edge nodes.

mira: Ops-bot, do we have any edge nodes showing discrepancy in the cached IdP cert fingerprint?

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Querying cert-fingerprint cache...

ops-bot: Node edge-7: fingerprint 0x9A3F... (current)
ops-bot: Node edge-3: fingerprint 0x8B2C... (stale) -> 429 migrations pending

alex: edge-3 bad. That explains signature verification mismatch. But still unclear about KMS decrypt error in SCIM.

jordan: If user matching fails because NameID format shifted (or mapping broke), SCIM might try to decrypt an external_id encrypted blob referencing a different KMS context. Our KMS unwrap path validates the key alias + header (tenant id). If the tenant mapping changed because of provisioning mismatch, unwrap fails.

mira: Workplan: 1) Roll cert cache on edge-3 (force refresh), 2) surface full SAML Assertion + SignatureMethod to confirm alg, 3) re-run failed SCIM deprovision for a sample tenant in dry-run mode.

sam: I can run (3) if ops gives node access. For dry-run use: 

sam: ```bash
curl -X POST https://scim.prod/repro/deprov-dryrun -d '{"user":"abc-uid-123","tenant":"acme-corp"}' -H 'Authorization: ReproToken'
```

ops-bot: edge-3 cache refresh queued. Rolling now... :arrows_counterclockwise:

ops-bot: edge-3 cert cache refreshed at 02:05 UTC. New fingerprint: 0x9A3F...

alex: After refresh, initial test login from acme-corp succeeded. No signature error. SCIM dry-run still returned decrypt error though.

mira: Run debug log with KMS context printing (PII redacted) and enable verbose SCIM trace for that tenant. We need the wrappedKey header and alias that KMS sees.

sam: Posted SCIM debug snippet: 

sam: ```
SCIM: deprov request tenant=acme-corp user=abc-uid-123
KMS: unwrap request alias=projects/prod/keys/tenant-acme keyHeader={"alg":"RSA-OAEP","ctx":"tenant:acme"}
KMS: unwrap error: context mismatch: expected tenant:acme-corp
```

jordan: There's the mismatch. Some code path is still using old short tenant id (acme) vs canonical acme-corp. That explains invalid header. Was there an RBAC rename recently? I recall a migration where we normalized tenant IDs and added suffixes.

alex: Yep — last week Platform did a rolling rename for several tenants to avoid collisions: acme -> acme-corp. The KMS headers used by older wrapped keys kept the old ctx. Most services can handle alias translation but apparently SCIM unwrap didn't check the translation map.

mira: OK, immediate mitigation: add a temporary KMS header alias hook in SCIM to accept old ctx values for unwrap. Longer-term: backfill wrapped keys with canonical context or store mapping in kms-compat layer.

sam: Patch ready, testing now with dry-run...

sam: Patch result: dry-run success, actual deprov replay in staging passes. No more decrypt error. :tada:

alex: Nice. Follow-ups: 
- Create an audit log of all tenants that still have wrapped keys with old ctx (for compliance).
- Add a small migration job to rewrap keys under canonical context.
- Add a guard in provisioning to fail faster with better metric (instead of 403 + generic decrypt error).

jordan: I'll open an RFC for the rewrap migration and RBAC rename fallout. Also put postmortem notes: edge cache staleness + tenant-id mismatch + missing compatibility in SCIM KMS client.

mira: Great. Anyone from legal/compliance want a heads-up about the migration/audit? Might need to keep audit trail of key rewrap operations.

alex: I'll ping legal + compliance with the audit plan later today. For now, marking this thread resolved but keeping it pinned until we land the rewrap job.

ops-bot: Incident tag: SSO-SCIM-KMS-2026-03-20 status=mitigated, owner=alex, followups=RFC-1427, rewrap-migration"
